subject: Re: [knitr] knitr and code width in beamer frames

messages.author: 30b406a9189eeb25
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] knitr and code width in beamer frames
parts:
Hi Jarrett,

Sure, I think you just want to change the width options of tidy.
add the command:

options(width = 75)

into your first chunk and that should do it.

(the option tidy=true is set on chunks be default, and linewraps at 72
characters, which is often too wide for slides).

-Carl

On Mon, Sep 3, 2012 at 1:05 PM, Jarrett Byrnes <jarrett...@gmail.com> wrote:
> I've been playing around with knitr and beamer, and enjoyed it. However, I
> get some funky results when the output is long. For example
>
>>
>> \documentclass{beamer}
>> \begin{document}
>> <<setup, include=FALSE>>=
>> # smaller font size for chunks
>> opts_chunk$set(size = 'footnotesize')
>> @
>> \begin{frame}[fragile]
>> \frametitle{test}
>>
>> <<a-frame>>=
>> rnorm(30)
>> @
>> \end{frame}
>> \end{document}
>
>
>
> produces a single slide, but the numbers from the R output are wider than
> the grey background. I've tried playing around with out.width, but to no
> avail.
>
> Note, without the opts_chunk setting, the entire output far overruns the
> width of the frame. Again, out.width didn't really help. Note, I'm running
> this with knitr 0.7 with R 2.15.1 in R-studio 0.96.331
>
> Are there any general solutions to these problems? Or even a good guide as
> to what to put in that preamble to make things look a-ok? Thanks!
>
> -Jarrett



--

messages.author: cc1ef8c8158d6b73
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] knitr and code width in beamer frames
parts:
75 is the default, which is too wide in beamer slides; I guess
options(width = 60) probably works...

The chunk option out.width only controls the width of figures;
options(width) deals with the width of text output.

Regards,
Yihui
